scenes.heading: A CAST IN *ONE SCRIPT*
scenes.say: One script, a whole cast of characters, each with their own voice.

scenes.heading: MEET *DRAMA 3*
scenes.say: This is Drama three from Fish Audio, a speech model built for scenes, not just narration.

scenes.heading: ONE TEXT, *16 VOICES*
scenes.label: characters in a single text
scenes.say: A single text can carry sixteen different characters, each tagged in the script.

scenes.heading: DIRECT THE *SCENE*
steps: Clone a voice from a clip
scenes.say: Tag each speaker, drop in directions like sighs and laughs, or clone a voice from a short clip.

scenes.heading: SERVE IT *YOURSELF*
scenes.say: Serve it with S G Lang Omni from day one, or try it in Fish Audio's playground.

scenes.heading: BEFORE YOU *CAST IT*
scenes.say: The catches: self-hosting wants a serious graphics card, and the licence is Fish Audio's community terms, not Apache. In return, edits are just rewrites, and the first audio lands fast.
What scene would you voice first? Comment DRAMA and I will pin the model card.

Fish Audio's Drama 3 is a 35B (3B active) text-to-speech model built for multi-character scenes: speaker tags carry up to 16 characters in one text, with voice cloning and in-line direction tags like [sighs] and [laughs]. Fish Audio Community License. Catches: self-hosting needs a serious GPU; vendor streaming figures were measured on an H200.
Source: https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3
